additional_requirements: depressive_episode is present for the majority of the total duration of the active and residual portions of the illness (Criterion C)
delusions_and_hallucinations occur for 2 or more weeks in the absence of a major mood episode (Criterion B)

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S021.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
S021.description: Symptoms where speech or thought appears scattered and difficult to follow due to a lack of logical or consistent flow.

subtypes.Derailment or Loose Associations: A speech pattern of switching rapidly from one topic to another with no logical connection between thoughts.
subtypes.Tangentiality: Speech that deviates entirely from the question and fails to answer directly.
subtypes.Incoherence or Word Salad: Severe fragmentation of speech and sentence structure, making it nearly impossible to understand.
subtypes.Neologisms: Using made-up words that have meaning only to the individual.
subtypes.Clang Associations: Speech governed by sounds, such as rhyming, rather than the meaning of words.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

symptom.disease_info: Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) is characterized by a continuous period of illness during which there is a major depressive episode concurrent with Criterion A symptoms of schizophrenia (delusions, hallucinations, disorganized thinking/behavior, and/or negative symptoms). There must be at least two weeks of psychotic symptoms occurring in the absence of prominent mood symptoms, distinguishing it from mood disorders with psychotic features, while mood episodes are present for the majority of the total duration of the illness, differentiating it from schizophrenia. The clinical course is typically chronic or relapsing, with variable functional impairment across work, relationships, and self-care, and onset can be linked to psychosocial stressors, health declines, or cumulative vulnerabilities. Depressive-type presentations often feature profound hopelessness and suicidality alongside the psychotic process, increasing risk for self-harm and delayed help-seeking.

patient.personality: A curious, creatively minded tech veteran who values flexibility and quirky projects, but tends to be laid-back and intermittently disorganized in his routines.
patient.stressor: About a year and a half ago, Russell’s long-time contract with a local manufacturing firm was abruptly not renewed after a major ERP migration, leaving him feeling professionally discarded and increasingly anxious about his relevance in a rapidly changing tech landscape. At the same time, he found it harder to keep up with complex projects and multitasking demands, which he interpreted as evidence that his mind was "slipping," amplifying longstanding insecurities from an earlier divorce and a sense of aging out of the field he loved. As he withdrew from consulting opportunities, his days became unstructured, dominated by solitary tinkering with vintage machines and late-night online deep dives, during which his thinking grew more rigid and preoccupied, and his worldview gradually took on an increasingly dark, self-referential tone. Over the ensuing months, his creative pursuits lost their usual pleasure, his functioning eroded to the point of neglecting basic responsibilities, and he ultimately sought psychiatric care after frightening himself with how often he found himself planning ways not to wake up rather than face what he was convinced was a pointless, deteriorating future.
patient.chief_complaint: I keep thinking about dying and different ways I could end my life, and it scares me how often that’s on my mind now.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: Over the past year I’ve become completely convinced that the big software companies and even my old client rigged the ERP system to watch me specifically, like they embedded some kind of tracking code in my old projects to monitor how useless I’ve become, and no matter how many times my son says, “Dad, that’s impossible,” it still feels absolutely true to me when I’m sitting alone at my desk at night seeing all these little ‘signs’ in error messages and update logs that seem aimed right at me.

S021.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
S021.description: Symptoms where speech or thought appears scattered and difficult to follow due to a lack of logical or consistent flow.
S021.manifestation: My thoughts used to line up like clean code, but now when I try to explain something—even just what I did that morning—I start off on the topic and then suddenly I’m talking about some old project, then the divorce, then microchips in supermarket scanners, and halfway through I realize I never actually answered the question and I can’t figure out how to get back to the point.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.
S022.manifestation: Some days I’ll just pace tight circles around my tiny home office for hours, muttering half-finished sentences about backups and ‘them’ listening, fiddling with cables and opening and closing the same laptops without actually doing anything, like my body is running on some jittery loop I can’t switch off even though I know it looks bizarre if anyone sees me.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most of the time now I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling like I’m already defeated before I’ve even had coffee, and the whole day has this flat, hopeless tone to it where I catch myself thinking, “You’re done, Russ, there’s nothing left to look forward to,” and I just kind of sink into that until it’s time to go back to bed.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to get a kick out of resurrecting old machines or taking on weird little coding puzzles, but for months I’ve been staring at half-disassembled towers and unfinished scripts on my desk and I just don’t care enough to touch them, and when friends email about grabbing a beer or a meetup I either ignore it or make an excuse because the idea of trying to act interested in anything feels exhausting and pointless.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: I used to be a guy who never skipped a meal, but over the last year my appetite has mostly vanished—whole days go by where I realize at 8 p.m. that all I’ve had is coffee and maybe a piece of toast, and even then I have to force myself to eat because food just tastes like cardboard and I’ve watched my belt notch creep tighter without really trying.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.
S028.manifestation: Lately it feels like my body is moving through molasses—if I’m sitting in my chair and decide I should get up to shower or make a sandwich, I just sit there staring at the floor for ten, fifteen minutes before I can even start to stand, and when I walk down the hall I’m shuffling so slowly it’s like I’m twice my age, with my words coming out just as sluggish when someone asks me something on the phone.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: Even simple stuff like paying a bill online or reading a short tech article has become weirdly hard—I’ll sit there rereading the same paragraph or staring at the payment screen, unable to decide what to click, my mind fogging over until I give up and tell myself I’ll deal with it later, and of course later never comes so everything piles up and makes me feel even more useless.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: For a long time now, pretty much every night as I’m lying in bed, my brain starts running through different ways I could make sure I don’t wake up—pills, the garage, the train tracks—and I’ll catch myself checking how many refills I have left or looking up lethal doses like I’m planning a project, and that cold, methodical part of it honestly scares me because a big part of me doesn’t see the point of sticking around anymore.
